properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation composed of Lower Carboniferous sedimentary sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone of the Strathclyde and Inverclyde Groups, overlain by dense glacial till. Primary structural lithic is pale buff to light-grey Craigleith quartzose sandstone, supplemented with brown-buff Hailes laminated sandstone for basement retaining walls and rear elevations. Mortar consists of traditional hot-mixed calcitic lime and sharp river sand aggregate.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Central garden enclosure planted with mature specimen broadleaf urban trees: Sycamore (*Acer pseudoplatanus*), Common Lime (*Tilia × europaea*), and Wych Elm (*Ulmus glabra*). Large ascending trunks with dense multi-tiered ramification, spreading spherical and ovate canopy volumes ranging from 12 to 22 meters in height, rooted in maintained turf with gravel path networks.

properties.architectural_summary: Moray Estate late-Georgian Neoclassical crescent and circus urbanism designed by James Gillespie Graham (c. 1822–1824). Symmetrical palace-fronted curving terrace: four-storey and basement continuous ashlar facades with pitched attic storeys behind parapets. Ground floor treated with horizontal channeled rustication and segmental-arched or square-headed openings. Piano nobile and upper floors feature smooth ashlar, molded architraves, continuous string courses, and mutule cornice surmounted by a stone blocking course. Slate-clad mansard and pitched roofs punctuated by regularly spaced gabled and segmental-headed timber-framed dormers; regular rhythm of stone-coped ashlar chimney stacks with earthenware cylindrical flues. Fenestration is timber sash-and-case in 6-over-6 and 12-over-12 configurations. Sunk basement lightwells protected by spearhead cast-iron balustrades. In the distant skyline, a classical octagonal drum and ribbed dome clad in standing-seam copper.
